item.title: The Gelfand triple and the weak Laplacian
item.description: Abstract. The classical Laplacian asks for two derivatives, but weak solutions of elliptic and parabolic equations often possess only one square-integrable derivative. This post develops the canonical Gelfand triple $H_0^1(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega) \hookrightarrow H^{-1}(\Omega)$ from first principles. We explain what each embedding means, construct the weak Dirichlet Laplacian as a bounded map from $H_0^1(\Omega)$ to $H^{-1}(\Omega)$, distinguish it from the unbounded Laplacian on $L^2(\Omega)$, and show why this framework is natural for the Poisson and heat equations.
